---
title: Get started
description: Install Console, connect an MCP client, and run an analysis.
---

Console runs on the same host as your MCP client.
For remote work, run both on the remote host, alongside the client's shell and filesystem tools.
Console does not manage remote connections or containers.

## Install

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), then install Console:

```sh
uv tool install mcp-console
```

PyPI provides wheels for macOS and Linux on ARM64 and x86-64, plus experimental Windows x64 support.
See [Windows local execution](WINDOWS.md) for native sandbox setup and platform limits.
Linux wheels require glibc 2.35 or later.
On Ubuntu, install the runtime libraries:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y libcap2 libgcc-s1 libstdc++6
```

Linux hosts must permit the namespace operations used by the native sandbox; see [Linux host compatibility](LINUX_COMPATIBILITY.md#host-and-container-setup).
On first startup, Console may download Python, packages, and DuckDB extensions.
To use R, install it separately, for example with [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig#id-installation) and `rig add release`.
Python and SQL also work without R.

### Build from source

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), Git, and [Rust through rustup](https://rustup.rs/).
The Rust compiler must meet the version requirement in [`Cargo.toml`](../Cargo.toml).
Console builds from source, so it also needs platform build tools.

On macOS, install the Xcode Command Line Tools:

```sh
xcode-select --install
```

On Ubuntu, install the build tools and system libraries:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential git pkg-config libcap-dev libssl-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev binutils
```

Windows users should follow [Windows build instructions](WINDOWS.md#build-from-source).
Package source builds can require additional system libraries; the [release guide](../RELEASE.md#private-sandbox-executable) covers native build requirements.

Install Console:

```sh
uv tool install git+https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console
```

This command builds Console and its sandbox runner from source.

## Connect your client

Register Console with Codex or Claude Code:

```sh
uvx mcp-console configure-client codex
uvx mcp-console configure-client claude
```

Choose the client you use, or pass both names to configure both clients in one command.
Inside a Git repository, it writes project configuration at the repository root; elsewhere, it writes global configuration.
Use `--scope project` or `--scope global` to choose explicitly.
The command prints the settings it writes, and `--dry-run` previews them without changing files.
By default, it also configures Console tools to load up front; `--no-auto-load` keeps the client's default discovery.
Restart the client and approve project configuration if prompted.
The default launch command is `uvx mcp-console serve`, with no version constraint.
Use `--pin-version v0.0.5` to select an exact version or `--pin-version latest` to request the latest release at launch.
Use `--pin-version current` to pin the version running setup.
Use `--no-uvx` to configure an absolute executable path; a temporary uvx run first installs its version persistently with uv.
See [client configuration](CLI.md#configure-a-client) for paths and visibility settings.

For other clients, configure a stdio MCP server with command `uvx` and arguments `["mcp-console", "serve"]`.
For an `mcpServers` mapping:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "console": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-console", "serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

`uvx mcp-console serve` runs the published package.
When reviewing a source installation, run that installation's `mcp-console configure-client CLIENT --no-uvx` to save its absolute executable path.

Confirm that the client exposes `send`.
Tool discovery can finish before runtime preparation; the first call may report that work is still running.
Let the agent collect that result rather than submit the code again.

## Try an analysis

Ask your agent:

> Use MCP Console to generate a small dataset with NumPy and pandas, fit a simple model, and plot the result.
> Keep the data and model for follow-up.

Then ask:

> Which observations does the model fit poorly?
> Show a plot and the path to the recorded session.

With R installed, try the Palmer Penguins data from `palmerpenguins`, summarize it with SQL, and plot it from Python.
The [runtime guide](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) explains the language bridges.

## Choose permissions and an environment

No configuration file is required.
The default sandbox allows host reads, but not ordinary workspace writes or direct network access.
It does not protect readable secrets.

For workspace writes, create `.agents/console/config.yaml` in the launch directory:

```yaml
sandbox:
  filesystem:
    read_write: [.]
```

To use an existing project Python environment rather than a Console-managed one, add:

```yaml
python: .venv
```

That environment must already contain the required packages.
See [Configuration](CONFIGURATION.md) for global/project layering and runtime selection, and [Sandbox configuration](SANDBOX_CONFIGURATION.md) for permissions.
Do not load configuration from an unfamiliar project without reviewing it; `--no-project-config` skips that layer.

## Keep the session

Console records transcripts and artifacts locally.
Read [Recordings and reports](RECORDING.md) for their location and how to turn a reviewed copy into a report.
Recordings are not checkpoints, contain input and output without redaction, and are not automatically deleted.
